attempted_claim: Fix an integer d >= 5 and a non-hyperelliptic Rauzy class R of irreducible permutations on d letters with genus g(R) > 1; fix pi in R that is not a circle rotation and satisfies (1,...,1) in H(pi), where H(pi) is the Veech homology space. Let P_+^{d-1} be the projective simplex of length data and f([lambda],pi) the d-interval exchange transformation. Let E_ue(pi) = {[lambda] in P_+^{d-1} : f([lambda],pi) is uniquely ergodic and not weakly mixing w.r.t. Lebesgue}. Prove, unconditionally and as an exact dimension identity, that HDim E_ue(pi) = d - 3/2 (Hausdorff codimension 1/2 in P_+^{d-1}), by establishing both sides through Rauzy-Veech renormalization: (i) HDim E_ue(pi) <= d - 3/2 via Zorich acceleration, fast-decay/large-deviation and contraction-hypothesis estimates for the Veech-criterion weak-stable lamination; and (ii) HDim E_ue(pi) >= d - 3/2 via an explicit staged freedom/restriction Rauzy-Veech matrix construction whose limit simplex consists of uniquely ergodic, non-weakly-mixing IETs and satisfies the illumination/diameter hypotheses.
decisive_failure: Both sides of the exact dimension identity are blocked by the same missing theorem: a Zorich fast-decay and large-deviation estimate uniform over the singular Veech-criterion weak-stable leaves, plus a verified staged Rauzy-Veech construction simultaneously enforcing eigenvalue alignment, unique ergodicity, and illumination bounds. The d=5 probe is illustrative only and proves no general bound.
